classes.def: A group of your students. Giving tests, marking and seeing scores all happen inside a class.

library.def: Where the tests, flashcard sets and grammar topics you write are kept. Write once, give to many classes.

assignments.def: The list of tests already given to the class. This section is inside each class.

semester.def: A class's school term. Students only see the work of the semester that is chosen.

assign.def: Hand a test from the {{library}} to the class. Until you do, students cannot see it.

deadline.def: The time a test opens and closes. After it closes, students cannot take it any more.

release.def: Students only see scores after you let them. Until then, only you can see them.

provisional.def: A score that only counts what the computer marked, because some written answers are not marked yet. It changes when you finish.

teacher.heading: Guide for teachers
teacher.intro: This page shows, step by step, how to do the common jobs. Text too small? Press {{textSize}} at the top of the page.
teacher.stuck: Still stuck? Ask the person in charge of IT at your school.

first.title: Your first visit
first.intro: You only need to do this once.
first.s1: Open the school website in your browser (Chrome or Cốc Cốc).
first.s2: Press {{login}} in the top right corner.
first.s3: Type the {{email}} and {{password}} the school gave you, then press {{submit}}.
first.s4: You will see the {{classes}} page, where your classes are.
first.s5: Text too small? Press {{textSize}} at the top of the page. Each press changes the size: large, very large, then back to normal.
first.s6: Forgot how to do something? Press {{help}} at the top of the page to open this guide again.
first.note: No email and password yet? Ask the person in charge of IT at your school.

classes.title: Create a class and add students
classes.intro: Every class has its own list of students.
classes.c1: Press {{classes}} at the top of the page.
classes.c4: Check that {{semester}} is right (it is usually already chosen).
classes.a1: Click the class you just created.
classes.a4: A few students: press {{one}}, type the name and email, then press {{submit}}.
classes.a5: The whole class: press {{excel}}, press {{template}}, fill in each student's name and email in the file, then press {{choose}} to pick the file and press {{confirm}}.
classes.p1: When it is done, the screen shows a table with each student's name, email and password.
classes.p3: Open the file, print it or copy from it, and hand each student theirs. Students log in with that email and password.
classes.f1: Open that student's class and press the {{students}} section.
classes.f2: Find the student's name and press {{reset}}.
classes.f4: Press {{copy}} to copy the new password, then give it to the student.
classes.note: A password is shown only once. Closed the window without saving? Follow "A student forgot the password" above to make a new one.

author.title: Write a test
author.intro: The computer saves every change, so you never need to press a Save button.
author.c1: Press {{library}} at the top of the page.
author.c3: Type the name of the test in {{title}}.
author.q1: Type {{sectionName}} (for example: Reading), then press {{addSection}}. Each group gathers questions of one kind.
author.q2: Inside the group, press {{multipleChoice}} to add a multiple-choice question, or {{essay}} to add a written question.
author.q3: Type the question. For multiple choice, type the choices and mark the right answer.
author.q4: It saves by itself. When you see {{saved}}, it is saved.
author.f1: Press {{preview}} to see the test the way students will.
author.note: {{variants}} are made by the computer when you give the test. You do not need to do anything.

assign.title: Give a test to a class and set a deadline
assign.intro: Students only see a test after you give it to them.
assign.s4: Click the square in front of a test's name to choose it.
assign.s6: Press {{week}}, or type a date and time in {{closeAt}}.
assign.noteDeadline: Want to change the deadline later? On the test you gave, press {{schedule}}.
assign.noteSemester: Students only see the work of the semester chosen in {{semester}} (top right of the class page).

grading.title: Grade the students' written answers
grading.intro: The computer marks multiple-choice questions. Only written (essay) answers need you.
grading.s1: Open the class and press the {{overview}} section.
grading.s2: Find {{needsGrading}}. These are the written answers waiting for you.
grading.s3: Press {{grade}} on the one you want to mark.
grading.s4: Read the student's answer, then type the score in {{score}}.
grading.s5: Press {{saveNext}} to go to the next student's answer, or {{save}} if you only want to mark this one.
grading.note: A test with written answers still unmarked is shown as {{provisional}} until you finish.

release.title: Let students see their scores
release.intro: Students cannot see scores until you let them.
release.s1: Open the class and press the {{assignments}} section.
release.s3: The screen asks once more. Press {{confirm}}.
release.s4: Want to hide the scores again? Press {{hide}}.
release.note: Do not want to press anything? When you give the test, choose {{auto}} (you need to set a deadline).

grades.title: See the gradebook and download the Excel scores
grades.intro: The gradebook shows the whole class's scores on one page.
grades.s1: Open the class and press the {{grades}} section.
grades.s2: Each row is a student and each column is a test.
grades.s3: Click a student's score to see their work.
grades.s4: Press {{export}} to download an Excel file.

announcements.title: Post an announcement to the class
announcements.intro: The announcement shows right on the students' page.
announcements.s1: Open the class and press the {{announcements}} section.
announcements.s2: Type your message in the {{composer}} box.
announcements.s3: To keep it on top, tick {{pin}}.
announcements.s5: To change or delete one: press {{edit}} or {{delete}} on that announcement.

student.heading: Guide for students
student.intro: Text too small? Press {{textSize}} at the top of the page.

todo.title: Find your work
todo.s1: Press {{assignments}} at the top of the page.
todo.s2: Work you can do right now is under {{open}}.
todo.s3: Look at the deadline under the test name to see when it is due.

doTest.title: Do a test and hand it in
doTest.s1: Press {{start}} on the test you choose.
doTest.s2: Choose or write an answer for each question. The computer saves it for you.
doTest.s3: Did not finish? Next time press {{resume}} to carry on.
doTest.s4: When you are done, press {{submit}}. You cannot change it after handing in.

grades.title: See your scores
grades.s1: Press {{grades}} at the top of the page.
grades.s2: A score shows after your teacher lets you see it. Before that you will see {{waiting}}.
grades.s3: To look at your work again, press {{viewResult}}.

vocab.title: Learn with flashcards
vocab.s1: Press {{flashcards}} at the top of the page.
vocab.s3: Learn the words in the set, then try the practice exercises.

news.title: See announcements and deadlines
news.s1: Your teacher's messages are on the {{assignments}} page, under {{announcements}}.
news.s2: Press the {{bell}} bell at the top of the page to see new work and work closing soon.
news.s3: In the bell, press {{calendar}} to see when each test is due.

aiGrading.heading: AI essay/writing & speaking grading
aiGrading.subtitle: Point AI grading of Essay/Writing and Speaking answers at any OpenAI-compatible API endpoint (one shared connection, below), and edit each grading prompt — no code change or server restart needed. While a toggle is off, or the connection isn't fully configured, that answer type falls back to the built-in heuristic grader.
aiGrading.essayPromptLabel: Essay/Writing grading prompt (system instructions sent to the AI)
aiGrading.systemPromptHint: Sent to the AI before every essay/writing answer. The built-in default is a condensed IELTS Writing band-descriptor rubric — edit it to change grading standards, tone, or language, with no code change.
aiGrading.speakingPromptLabel: Speaking grading prompt (system instructions sent to the AI)
aiGrading.speakingPromptHint: Sent to the AI along with the candidate's actual recorded audio before every speaking answer. The built-in default is a condensed IELTS Speaking band-descriptor rubric — edit it to change grading standards, tone, or language, with no code change.
